strengths: Clear empirical observation that reasoning uncertainty is localized to high-entropy tokens, well-demonstrated in Figure 1
Practical training-free method that adds minimal inference overhead (only 4-25% of tokens require CFG)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse benchmarks (general, coding, math/science), multiple model scales (8B-32B), and both base/reasoning variants
Thorough ablation studies and analysis including entropy threshold effects, CFG strength tuning, prompt variants, and principled justification for entropy-based selection (Figure 5)
Well-written paper with effective visualizations and clear presentation of the core concepts
weaknesses: Limited novelty: combines established techniques (entropy-based selection from Li et al. 2025/Wang et al. 2025, CFG from Ho & Salimans 2022, LLM-CFG from Sanchez et al. 2023); main contribution is incremental combination

Concerning vanilla CFG baseline: frequently underperforms direct inference (e.g., Qwen3-8B-Base MMLU-Pro: 50.28 vs 56.81, Qwen3-14B-Reasoning WinoGrande: 66.22 vs 75.14), raising questions about implementation correctness and whether improvements stem from selective intervention or VC failures

Modest empirical improvements: averages of 0.39-1.8% across model variants; only specialized benchmarks show larger gains (e.g., GPQA-Diamond +6.57); most results are single-run without error bars or statistical significance testing

Hyperparameter sensitivity undermines practical applicability: entropy threshold τ varies per model type (1.5 for base vs 1.0 for reasoning) with non-monotonic behavior; CFG strength ω requires tuning; no principled guidance for selecting hyperparameters on new models

Lack of theoretical justification: 'OUTPUT ERROR' design appears ad-hoc (why these words?); explanation that it 'constructs more informative unconditional space' is vague; limited systematic exploration of prompt variants (only 4 in Figure 3c)

Technical clarity gaps: KV-cache reuse mechanism poorly explained (are separate forward passes needed? how does this differ computationally from vanilla CFG?); Equation 1 uses log probabilities while typical LLM-CFG manipulates logits directly; uncertainty threshold application strategy unclear
Limited analysis of failure modes: no discussion of when MTI underperforms or hurts accuracy; no per-domain analysis of which tasks benefit most/least
Incomplete stochastic sampling evaluation: main results use greedy decoding; stochastic sampling results only for AIME2024 despite modern systems using sampling
Missing comparisons with other selective guidance methods, entropy-aware approaches, or recent test-time reasoning strategies

strengths: Clear and well-motivated core insight: High-entropy tokens concentrate errors in LLM reasoning, with compelling empirical evidence in Figure 1. This observation is intuitive and strongly supported.
Practical efficiency design: KV-cache reuse via negative-prompt injection cleverly avoids dual-cache overhead of standard CFG while remaining compatible with modern inference frameworks (vLLM).

Comprehensive empirical validation: Experiments span multiple model families (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1, Ling-mini), diverse benchmarks across general/coding/STEM categories, and even extension to VLMs. Comparison with SOTA methods (Table 5) shows competitive performance.

Thorough ablation studies: Systematic analysis of entropy threshold τ, CFG hyperparameter ω, negative prompt semantics, and correlation between token entropy and CFG effectiveness (Figure 4). Clear unimodal patterns enable principled threshold selection.

Insightful supplementary analysis: Word-cloud visualization (Figure 5) reveals lexical diversity improvements; case studies (Figure 6) illustrate concrete advantages over vanilla CFG (e.g., avoiding repetitive loops). Analysis of entropy scopes (Table 6) clarifies why selective intervention matters.

Reproducibility and clarity: Implementation details provided, OpenCompass configuration files specified, code availability mentioned. Generally clear writing with good motivation and effective visualizations.
weaknesses: Weak theoretical justification for negative-prompt mechanism: The paper assumes that prepending 'OUTPUT ERROR' to conditional KV cache effectively approximates unconditional distributions but provides no formal analysis or empirical validation of approximation quality. What distribution is actually being computed? How close is it to true unconditional?

Overstated efficiency claims: Table 3 shows MTI latency is often not better than DI (6081s for Qwen-14B vs. 4547s for DI). Claims of 'minimal overhead' and 'negligible computational overhead' are contradicted by mixed results. Shorter outputs confound method efficiency with task difficulty.

Hyperparameter tuning requirement contradicts parameter-free claims: Despite claiming robustness without 'meticulous tuning,' entropy threshold τ still requires cross-validation with clear unimodal patterns. Section 6 acknowledges needing 'a small subset of data to sweep for τ'—this is parameter tuning. No principled method provided for threshold selection without validation data.

Insufficient analysis of vanilla CFG underperformance: VC severely underperforms in many cases (e.g., 29.29%→32.32% on GPQA-Diamond). Why does standard CFG fail so dramatically? Possible implementation issues? This undermines the fairness of comparisons and raises questions about the baseline.

Negative prompt semantics still somewhat arbitrary: While 'OUTPUT ERROR' generalizes, Table 8 shows task-specific prompts are notably better (94.20% vs. 93.60% for math). The paper doesn't explain mechanistically why negative prompting works or explore design space thoroughly. Is this exploiting model artifacts?

Limited theoretical novelty: Core components (CFG, entropy-based selection) exist individually. Main contribution is selective application + KV-reuse, which is practical but conceptually incremental. Limited new insights into LLM reasoning mechanisms.

Statistical rigor concerns: No confidence intervals, significance tests, or standard deviations reported. Some improvements are modest (+1.99% on VaBenchPoint). AIME2024 results show mean over 8 runs but no variance analysis. Unclear if improvements are statistically significant.

Scope limitations of main experiments: Table 1 uses only greedy search (reducing generalizability). Stochastic decoding only evaluated on AIME2024. Unclear interaction with other decoding strategies (beam search, nucleus sampling). Method tested only on recent models.

Superficial failure case analysis: Limitations section (Section 6) is brief and doesn't deeply explore when selective CFG might fail. No pathological case analysis. Figure 6 case study is illustrative but anecdotal. No discussion of when high-entropy tokens should NOT be modified.

Vanilla CFG comparison fairness unclear: Table 6 shows VC at 73.34% vs. DI at 73.75% on AIME2024 (essentially tied). If vanilla CFG barely underperforms DI, is the distinction between VC and MTI truly fundamental or just better tuning? Raises questions about comparison validity.
